projects_core.name: projects_core
projects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  -- monetary measures cast to numeric for canonical numeric type
  p.total_cost::numeric AS total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution::numeric AS ec_max_contribution,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  p.framework_program,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  p.acronym
FROM projects p
projects_core.description: Normalized projection of the projects table exposing primary identifiers, title and monetary measures with canonical numeric types and important timeline columns. Useful as the base row-level relation for any project-level filtering, aggregation or joins.
validated_on: Get acronyms of projects beginning in 2018
Find titles of projects which started earlier than 2016
Count the projects that started in 2016
Show me the title of projects which have an end year and a start year after 2006
Find the acronym of projects which have total costs between 100000 and 200000
Show the title of projects with costs higher than 1000000
Show the project title and member name where the member has a partner role

project_members_core.name: project_members_core
project_members_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id,
  pm.project,
  pm.member_name,
  pm.institution_id,
  pm.ec_contribution,
  pm.country,
  pm.member_role,
  pm.member_short_name
FROM project_members pm
project_members_core.description: Row-level projection of project_members exposing member, institution and contribution info per membership. Useful for filtering projects by members, institutions, countries, or summing contributions at project or member level.
validated_on: Find the id of projects with at least 100 members
Show me the all different names of people
counter_examples: Show the acronym of projects with a member from Greece

projects_with_programs_subjects_topics.name: projects_with_programs_subjects_topics
projects_with_programs_subjects_topics.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  pp.programme AS programme,
  psa.subject_area AS subject_area,
  pt.topic AS topic
FROM
  projects p
LEFT JOIN project_programmes pp ON pp.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_subject_areas psa ON psa.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN project_topics pt ON pt.project = p.unics_id
projects_with_programs_subjects_topics.description: Denormalized project-level view joining projects to their programmes, subject areas and topics. One row per project x (programme/subject/topic) combination; useful for filtering projects by programme, subject area, topic or for counting projects by those dimensions.

projects_financial_summary_by_project.name: projects_financial_summary_by_project
projects_financial_summary_by_project.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  p.total_cost AS project_total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution AS project_ec_max_contribution,
  COALESCE(SUM(pm.ec_contribution), 0) AS sum_member_ec_contribution,
  COUNT(pm.unics_id) FILTER (WHERE pm.unics_id IS NOT NULL) AS member_count
FROM
  projects_core p
LEFT JOIN
  project_members_core pm
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
GROUP BY
  p.unics_id,
  p.total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution
projects_financial_summary_by_project.description: Aggregated financial measures per project: sums of member EC contributions and project-reported total_cost/ec_max_contribution. Keeps one row per project for financial comparisons and validation.
counter_examples: Show the total costs of all projects

projects_core_4.name: projects_core_4
projects_core_4.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,
  p.start_year,

projects_core_4.description: Normalized, project-level canonical projection with key identifiers and primary timeline and funding columns. Clean projection (no aggregations) useful as the base cohort for time-based filters and joins to program/subjects/members.

project_acronym_timeline.name: project_acronym_timeline
project_acronym_timeline.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.start_date,
  p.start_year
FROM projects_core p
project_acronym_timeline.description: A small focused projection of project identifier, acronym and start_date/start_year for quick year-based cohort selection and text output. Useful for queries that return or filter by project acronym and start year.

project_with_program_and_scheme.name: project_with_program_and_scheme
project_with_program_and_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.start_date,
  -- lift literal nulls/defaults out of view: if no programme found, caller can supply filter; keep raw programme value
  pp.programme,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  p.ec_max_contribution,
  p.total_cost
FROM projects_core p
LEFT JOIN projects_with_programs_subjects_topics pp
  ON p.unics_id = pp.unics_id
project_with_program_and_scheme.description: Denormalized project row enriched with programme and funding scheme labels (joins to project_programmes and funding_schemes). One row per project; keeps raw measures and identifiers to support grouping/filters by programme or funding scheme.

project_time_cohort.name: project_time_cohort
project_time_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  -- prefer canonical acronym from projects_core_4 if available, else fallback to projects.acronym
  COALESCE(pc4.acronym, p.acronym) AS acronym,
  -- canonical start_date: prefer projects_core_4.start_date, then projects.start_date, then project_acronym_timeline.start_date
  COALESCE(pc4.start_date, p.start_date, pat.start_date) AS start_date,
  -- canonical start_year: prefer projects_core_4.start_year, then projects.start_year, then extract year from the canonical start_date
  COALESCE(pc4.start_year, p.start_year, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(pc4.start_date, p.start_date, pat.start_date))::integer) AS start_year
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN projects_core_4 pc4 USING (unics_id)
LEFT JOIN project_acronym_timeline pat USING (unics_id)
project_time_cohort.description: Cohort view selecting projects with a canonical start_date and year. Exposes start_date and derived year to support year-based filtering and grouping.

project_participants_joined.name: project_participants_joined
project_participants_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id                                                     AS "project_members.unics_id",
  pm.project                                                       AS "project_members.project",
  pm.member_name                                                   AS "project_members.member_name",
  pm.institution_id                                                AS "project_members.institution_id",
  i.unics_id                                                       AS "institutions.unics_id",
  i.institutions_name                                               AS "institutions.institutions_name",
  p.unics_id                                                       AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.acronym                                                        AS "projects.acronym",
  p.start_date                                                     AS "projects.start_date"
FROM
  project_members pm
LEFT JOIN institutions i
  ON pm.institution_id = i.unics_id
LEFT JOIN projects p
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_participants_joined.description: Denormalized view joining projects to their project_members and institutions to expose participant counts and institution attributes per project. Useful for queries that need participant/institution context alongside project acronyms and dates.

projects_rowlevel.name: projects_rowlevel
projects_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT

  p.ec_max_contribution AS ec_max_contribution,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator
FROM projects_core_4 p
projects_rowlevel.description: Row-level canonical view of projects exposing core identifiers, dates, costs and key attributes for filtering and joins.
validated_on: Count the projects that started in 2016

project_participants.name: project_participants
project_participants.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id",

projects_with_programme_subject_topic.name: projects_with_programme_subject_topic
projects_with_programme_subject_topic.body_sql:
SELECT
  pp.project AS "project_programmes.project",
  pp.programme AS "project_programmes.programme",

eu_territorial_units_lookup.name: eu_territorial_units_lookup
eu_territorial_units_lookup.body_sql:

eu_territorial_units_lookup.description: Lookup of EU territorial units keyed by geocode_regions, exposing the description and geocode level. Useful to map geocode region codes to human-readable region names for filtering and joining.

Show me the all different names of people

project_principal_investigators.name: project_principal_investigators
project_principal_investigators.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id                             AS project_unics_id,
  p.principal_investigator               AS principal_investigator,

LEFT JOIN
  people pe
ON
  pe.unics_id = p.principal_investigator
project_principal_investigators.description: Denormalized mapping of projects to their principal investigator person records; one row per project with associated PI id and PI full name (if available).

projects_core_15.name: projects_core_15
projects_core_15.body_sql:

SELECT

subject_areas_lookup.name: subject_areas_lookup

project_topics_link.name: project_topics_link

topics_canonical.name: topics_canonical
topics_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code AS code,
  NULLIF(trim(both ' ' FROM regexp_replace(t.title, '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')), '') AS title,
  t.rcn AS rcn
FROM topics t
topics_canonical.description: Canonical topic records with code and title (cleaned projection) for consistent labeling and easy selection of topic titles.
counter_examples: Show me topic titles which contain the word 'climate'

projects_with_members_denorm.name: projects_with_members_denorm
projects_with_members_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  p.acronym AS project_acronym,
  pm.unics_id AS member_unics_id,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.country AS member_country,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id
FROM
  projects_core p
JOIN
  project_members_core pm
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
projects_with_members_denorm.description: Denormalized rows joining projects to their members (one row per project-member) exposing project acronym and member country to support existence checks and groupings by member country.

institutions_with_country.name: institutions_with_country
institutions_with_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  institutions.unics_id AS "institutions.unics_id",
  institutions.institutions_name AS "institutions.institutions_name",
  institutions.country_id AS "institutions.country_id",
  countries.country_name AS "countries.country_name",
  countries.country_code2 AS "countries.country_code2",
  countries.country_code3 AS "countries.country_code3"
FROM
  institutions

  countries
ON
  institutions.country_id = countries.unics_id
institutions_with_country.description: Denormalized view joining institutions to their country row to enable filtering by country name and expose institution and country attributes together.

institutions_with_country_28.name: institutions_with_country_28
institutions_with_country_28.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id AS unics_id,
  i.institutions_name AS institutions_name,
  i.country_id AS country_id,
  c.country_name AS country_name,
  i.acronym AS acronym,
  i.short_name AS short_name,
  i.website AS website
FROM institutions i
LEFT JOIN countries c
  ON i.country_id = c.unics_id
institutions_with_country_28.description: Denormalized institutions rows joined to countries (left join) so institutions lacking a country row are preserved; exposes country_name for filtering (treat missing country as not matching specific country names).
counter_examples: Show me the country of all institutes.

project_participating_institutions.name: project_participating_institutions
project_participating_institutions.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS "projects.unics_id",
  p.start_date AS "projects.start_date",
  p.start_year AS "projects.start_year",
  pm.unics_id AS "project_members.unics_id",
  pm.institution_id AS "project_members.institution_id",
  pm.country AS "project_members.country"
FROM projects p
JOIN project_members pm
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_participating_institutions.description: Denormalized relation of project -> participating institution rows by joining projects to project_members and institutions. One row per project-member pairing exposing project id, project dates and member institution id and country for filtering and aggregations involving institutions per project.

projects_costs_for_ranking.name: projects_costs_for_ranking
projects_costs_for_ranking.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.total_cost,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY p.total_cost DESC NULLS LAST) AS total_cost_rank,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY p.total_cost DESC NULLS LAST) AS total_cost_dense_rank
FROM
  projects_core p
projects_costs_for_ranking.description: Per-project ranking and dense rank over total_cost to support top-k queries and ties. Exposes total_cost and rank measures alongside project id and title.

project_members_core_31.name: project_members_core_31
project_members_core_31.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id AS unics_id,
  pm.project AS project,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id,
  pm.ec_contribution AS ec_contribution,

  pm.latitude AS latitude,

FROM project_members pm
project_members_core_31.description: One-row-per-project-member canonical projection exposing membership keys, member identity, institution link, financial contribution and geographic fields for joining and filtering. Cleans nothing aggressively — preserves NULLs so downstream question_ops can exclude them.
validated_on: Show the project title and member name where the member has a partner role

project_members_with_project.name: project_members_with_project
project_members_with_project.body_sql:

  pm.project AS project,

  pm.ec_contribution AS ec_contribution,

projects_row_level.name: projects_row_level
projects_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT

projects_row_level.description: One row per project exposing project identifiers and basic attributes for joins to members and aggregation.

project_member_counts_by_project.name: project_member_counts_by_project
project_member_counts_by_project.body_sql:

  COUNT(pm.unics_id) AS member_count

  project_members_core pm

project_member_counts_by_project.description: Pre-aggregated counts of members per project (one row per project) to support filters like 'projects with at least N members'.

projects_row_level_35.name: projects_row_level_35
projects_row_level_35.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  -- lift literal/defaults out of view: use the ec_fund_scheme as stored in projects_core (nullable)
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date,

  p.end_year,
  p.total_cost,

FROM

projects_row_level_35.description: Canonical cleaned/projection view of projects at one row per project. Exposes project identifier and the funding scheme key used to link to funding_schemes, plus basic project date/cost fields useful for many aggregations.

funding_schemes_dim.name: funding_schemes_dim
funding_schemes_dim.body_sql:

  fs.title AS title
FROM funding_schemes fs
funding_schemes_dim.description: Dimension table projection for funding schemes: canonical code and human title. Useful for joining funding scheme codes on projects and for any reporting that needs scheme metadata.
validated_on: Find the code of the funding scheme for Framework Partnership Agreement

projects_by_funding_scheme.name: projects_by_funding_scheme
projects_by_funding_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  pc.ec_fund_scheme,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pc.unics_id) AS project_count
FROM
  projects_core pc
GROUP BY
  pc.ec_fund_scheme
projects_by_funding_scheme.description: Aggregate counts of projects per funding scheme code (one row per funding scheme code). Counts distinct projects and preserves the scheme code for joins to funding_schemes_dim for titles or other metadata.

project_membership.name: project_membership
project_membership.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.project AS project,
  p.unics_id AS projects_unics_id,
  pm.unics_id AS member_unics_id,
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.institution_id AS institution_id,
  pm.ec_contribution AS ec_contribution,
  pm.country AS country,
  pm.member_role AS member_role
FROM project_members pm
LEFT JOIN projects p
  ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_membership.description: Denormalized view linking projects to their members/institutions and basic member attributes. Useful for questions that filter/group by member country, institution or EC contribution.

projects_topic_subject_programme.name: projects_topic_subject_programme
projects_topic_subject_programme.body_sql:
SELECT
  pp.project AS project,
  pt.topic AS topic,
  psa.subject_area AS subject_area,
  pp.programme AS programme
FROM project_programmes pp
LEFT JOIN project_topics pt ON pt.project = pp.project
LEFT JOIN project_subject_areas psa ON psa.project = pp.project
projects_topic_subject_programme.description: Associates projects with their topics, subject areas and programmes. One row per (project, dimension) association to support filtering/grouping by topic/subject/programme.

projects_row_level_40.name: projects_row_level_40
projects_row_level_40.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  -- lift literals: keep raw start_year and end_year from source
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year,
  -- duration_years: prefer normalized integer years when available; compute from dates if years missing.
  -- Return NULL if neither start_year/end_year nor start_date/end_date provide duration.
  CASE
    WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL THEN (p.end_year - p.start_year)
    WHEN p.start_year IS NOT NULL AND p.end_year IS NULL AND p.start_date IS NOT NULL AND p.end_date IS NOT NULL THEN
      (EXTRACT(year FROM p.end_date)::integer - p.start_year)
    WHEN p.start_year IS NULL AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL AND p.start_date IS NOT NULL AND p.end_date IS NOT NULL THEN
      (p.end_year - EXTRACT(year FROM p.start_date)::integer)
    WHEN p.start_date IS NOT NULL AND p.end_date IS NOT NULL THEN
      (EXTRACT(year FROM p.end_date)::integer - EXTRACT(year FROM p.start_date)::integer)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS duration_years
FROM projects_core_4 p
projects_row_level_40.description: One row per project from the projects table with normalized numeric year fields and a prepared duration_years expression (not aggregated). Keeps raw start/end year columns and exposes key project attributes for filtering and joining.

projects_with_valid_years_cohort.name: projects_with_valid_years_cohort
projects_with_valid_years_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.start_year,
  p.end_year
FROM projects_core p
WHERE p.start_year IS NOT NULL
  AND p.end_year IS NOT NULL
projects_with_valid_years_cohort.description: Cohort of projects that have non-null start_year and end_year. Exposes project identifiers and the raw year columns so downstream queries can compute duration or group by year ranges.

topics_row_level.name: topics_row_level
topics_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code AS code,
  t.title AS title
FROM topics t
topics_row_level.description: Row-level cohort of topics; one row per topic code with its title and related identifiers. Useful as the base cohort for filtering topic titles or joining topic metadata.

projects_topics_join.name: projects_topics_join
projects_topics_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.project::integer AS project,
  pt.topic::text AS topic,
  t.title::text AS topic_title,
  p.unics_id::integer AS project_unics_id,
  p.acronym::text AS project_acronym
FROM
  project_topics pt
  JOIN projects p ON p.unics_id = pt.project
  LEFT JOIN topics t ON t.code = pt.topic
projects_topics_join.description: Denormalized relation joining projects to associated topics (many-to-many via project_topics). One row per project-topic association exposing project identifiers and topic metadata; useful for queries about projects by topic title or aggregations of projects per topic.

topic_titles_canonical.name: topic_titles_canonical
topic_titles_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.code AS code,
  t.title AS title,
  -- canonical title: trim surrounding whitespace and normalize internal spaces to single space
  regexp_replace(trim(t.title), '\s+', ' ', 'g') AS title_canonical
FROM topics t
topic_titles_canonical.description: Normalized view of topic titles: exposes topic code, raw title, and a trimmed/canonicalized title for consistent prefix/substring matching (whitespace trimmed). Keeps original title too. Useful for case-sensitive or trimmed comparisons.

projects_with_topics_join.name: projects_with_topics_join
projects_with_topics_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  p.acronym AS project_acronym,
  t.code AS topic_code,
  t.title AS topic_title
FROM projects p
JOIN project_topics pt ON pt.project = p.unics_id
LEFT JOIN topics t ON t.code = pt.topic
projects_with_topics_join.description: Denormalized relation linking projects to their topic codes and project metadata; one row per project-topic pairing to support questions that filter projects by topic text or aggregate projects by topic.

project_principal_investigator_assignmen.name: project_principal_investigator_assignments
project_principal_investigator_assignmen.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS project_unics_id,
  p.acronym AS project_acronym,
  p.title AS project_title,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator_unics_id,
  pi.full_name AS principal_investigator_full_name
FROM
  projects_core_4 p
LEFT JOIN
  people pi
ON
  p.principal_investigator = pi.unics_id
project_principal_investigator_assignmen.description: Denormalized mapping of projects to their principal investigator names and ids; one row per project (project-level assignment). Useful for counting projects per PI or filtering projects by PI name.

project_financials_summary.name: project_financials_summary
project_financials_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  -- lift literals: none for this view
  -- core financials: prefer projects_core if available, fall back to projects table via projects_core_4 consistency
  COALESCE(p.total_cost, pf.project_total_cost) AS total_cost,
  COALESCE(p.ec_max_contribution, pf.project_ec_max_contribution) AS ec_max_contribution,
  p.start_year AS start_year,
  p.end_year AS end_year
FROM projects_core p
LEFT JOIN projects_financial_summary_by_project pf
  ON pf.project_unics_id = p.unics_id
project_financials_summary.description: Per-project financial measures and basic timeline (keeps one row per project). Aggregates are trivial here (selects raw totals), but structured for reuse when adding more financial aggregates (e.g., summed contributions from members).

project_with_principal_investigator.name: project_with_principal_investigator
project_with_principal_investigator.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.acronym AS acronym,
  p.total_cost AS total_cost,
  p.principal_investigator AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name AS pi_full_name
FROM
  projects_core_4 p
LEFT JOIN
  people pe
ON
  p.principal_investigator = pe.unics_id
project_with_principal_investigator.description: Denormalized project rows joined to the principal investigator's person record (exposes project and PI identifiers and names). Useful for questions that filter or group by PI or need PI name alongside project attributes.

project_financials.name: project_financials
project_financials.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution,
  -- lift literal for safe division: if total_cost is NULL or zero, contribution_share is NULL
  CASE
    WHEN p.total_cost IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.total_cost = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE p.ec_max_contribution / p.total_cost
  END AS contribution_share
FROM projects p
project_financials.description: A focused projection of projects with key financial measures (total_cost, ec_max_contribution, ec_max_contribution / total_cost as contribution_share) to support cost-based filtering and ranking.

project_with_principal_investigator_50.name: project_with_principal_investigator_50
project_with_principal_investigator_50.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id::integer AS unics_id,
  p.title::text AS title,
  p.total_cost::double precision AS total_cost,
  p.principal_investigator::integer AS principal_investigator,
  pe.full_name::text AS pi_full_name
FROM
  projects_core_4 p
LEFT JOIN
  people pe
ON
  p.principal_investigator IS NOT NULL
  AND pe.unics_id = p.principal_investigator::integer
project_with_principal_investigator_50.description: Denormalized project rows joined with principal investigator name (people) and principal investigator id to enable questions that filter or display PI alongside project attributes.

projects_rowlevel_51.name: projects_rowlevel_51
projects_rowlevel_51.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id AS unics_id,
  p.title AS title,
  p.total_cost AS total_cost,
  p.ec_ref AS ec_ref,
  p.start_date AS start_date,
  p.end_date AS end_date,
  p.start_year AS start_year,
  p.end_year AS end_year,
  p.framework_program AS framework_program,
  p.acronym AS acronym
FROM projects p
projects_rowlevel_51.description: Canonical, row-level projection of the projects table exposing stable identifiers and raw numeric measures (no aggregation). Useful as the base cohort for filters like cost thresholds, year filters, or joins to other project-linked tables.

projects_with_program_and_pi.name: projects_with_program_and_pi
projects_with_program_and_pi.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.title,
  p.total_cost,
  pp.programme,
  p.principal_investigator
FROM
  projects_core_4 p
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT programme
  FROM projects_with_programs_subjects_topics pw
  WHERE pw.unics_id = p.unics_id
  UNION ALL
  -- if there is no programme row, return a single NULL to preserve project-level grain
  SELECT NULL::text
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM projects_with_programs_subjects_topics pw2 WHERE pw2.unics_id = p.unics_id
  )
  LIMIT 1
) pp ON true
projects_with_program_and_pi.description: Denormalized view linking projects to their programme(s) and principal investigator id (people/institutions can be joined by caller). One row per project-programme pairing (project-level grain can be kept with programme NULL if missing). Exposes project identifiers, title, cost and programme code for grouping or filtering by programme.

project_financials_by_year.name: project_financials_by_year
project_financials_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id::integer AS unics_id,
  -- lift year literals out: use project's own start_year and end_year
  p.start_year::integer AS start_year,
  p.end_year::integer AS end_year,
  -- raw financial measures from projects_core (prefer projects_core if available)
  p.total_cost::double precision AS total_cost,
  p.ec_max_contribution::double precision AS ec_max_contribution,
  -- percentage: ec_max_contribution / total_cost when total_cost > 0, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN p.total_cost IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p.total_cost = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (p.ec_max_contribution::double precision / p.total_cost::double precision) * 100.0
  END AS ec_max_contribution_pct
FROM
  projects_core p
project_financials_by_year.description: Aggregate financial measures for each project by start_year and end_year (raw measures not averaged). Useful for yearly rollups, time-window filters and comparisons. This view does NOT perform cross-project aggregation beyond grouping by project and years.

project_member_role_lookup.name: project_member_role_lookup
project_member_role_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.unics_id,
  pm.project,
  pm.member_name,
  pm.member_role,
  pmr.description AS member_role_description
FROM
  project_members pm
LEFT JOIN
  project_member_roles pmr
ON
  pm.member_role = pmr.code
project_member_role_lookup.description: Denormalized mapping between project_members and their role descriptions by joining project_members to project_member_roles. One row per project_members.unics_id with role code and role description.

institutions_with_country_55.name: institutions_with_country_55
institutions_with_country_55.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id,
  i.institutions_name,
  c.country_name
FROM
  institutions i
JOIN
  countries c
    ON i.country_id = c.unics_id
WHERE
  i.country_id IS NOT NULL
institutions_with_country_55.description: Denormalized institution rows enriched with their matched country name. Includes only institutions that have a non-NULL country_id and an existing matching country in countries.

institutions_base.name: institutions_base
institutions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.unics_id,
  i.institutions_name,
  i.country_id,
  i.geocode_regions_3,
  i.acronym,
  i.short_name,
  i.website,
  i.grid_id
FROM institutions i
institutions_base.description: Canonical one-row-per-institution projection exposing institution identifiers, name, country foreign key, region code and common contact/metadata columns. Keeps raw values (no aggregation) so it can be joined or filtered for reporting.

projects_with_funding_scheme.name: projects_with_funding_scheme
projects_with_funding_scheme.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.ec_fund_scheme,
  fs.title AS funding_scheme_title
FROM projects_core p
LEFT JOIN funding_schemes fs
  ON p.ec_fund_scheme = fs.code
projects_with_funding_scheme.description: Denormalized view joining projects to their funding scheme code and title so queries can filter or aggregate projects by funding scheme.

programmes_core.name: programmes_core
programmes_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonicalised textual fields lifted from programmes table
  trim(nullif(title, ''))::text AS title,
  trim(nullif(short_name, ''))::text AS short_name,
  code,
  trim(nullif(rcn, ''))::text AS rcn,
  trim(nullif(parent, ''))::text AS parent
FROM programmes
programmes_core.description: Canonicalised programme rows exposing programme identifiers and names. One row per programme; cleans/normalises textual fields for reuse (no filtering).

programme_shortname_index.name: programme_shortname_index
programme_shortname_index.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.code,
  p.short_name,
  p.title
FROM
  programmes p
WHERE
  -- lift literal for short_name search OUT of the view: caller should replace 'REPLACE_ME' with desired pattern
  -- examples: '= ''ABC''' or "ILIKE '%%something%%'"
  p.short_name IS NOT NULL
  AND ( /* replace the following predicate as needed by caller */
        p.short_name ILIKE 'REPLACE_ME'
      )
programme_shortname_index.description: Subset/cohort view to find programmes by short_name. One row per programme (same grain as programmes_core) to support lookups by short_name; keeps key columns and titles for direct selection.

project_members_core_60.name: project_members_core_60
project_members_core_60.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.project AS project
FROM
  project_members pm
project_members_core_60.description: One-row-per-project-member core cohort with member identifiers, contact/location, role and link to project

projects_identifiers.name: projects_identifiers
projects_identifiers.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.unics_id,
  -- lift literals: if caller wants to filter by acronym case-insensitively, they can supply their own literal; here we just pass through stored value
  p.acronym,
  p.title,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date
FROM projects_core_4 p
projects_identifiers.description: Project identifier and basic metadata for linking and filtering projects (acronym, unics_id, title, start/end)

project_members_with_project_62.name: project_members_with_project_62
project_members_with_project_62.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.member_name AS member_name,
  pm.member_role AS member_role,
  pm.project AS project,
  p.unics_id AS projects_unics_id,
  p.acronym AS projects_acronym
FROM project_members pm
LEFT JOIN projects p ON pm.project = p.unics_id
project_members_with_project_62.description: Denormalized join of project_members to projects to enable filtering members by project attributes (project acronym, title). One row per project_members.unics_id.
